nodes.name: Mopane
nodes.desc: The dominant tree of the hot valley floor, often forming near-uniform woodland. Its leaves feed elephants, giraffes, antelopes and caterpillars.

nodes.name: Floodplain grasses
nodes.desc: Grasslands among the woodland and on the seasonally flooded plains feed zebra, antelopes, buffalo and hippos.

nodes.name: Ebony tree
nodes.desc: Riverine forest tree whose fruit and leaves are eaten by elephants, impala and many other animals.

nodes.name: Water lettuce
nodes.desc: A floating plant of lagoons and slow water that is eaten by some antelopes.

nodes.name: Plains zebra
nodes.desc: A grazer of valley grasslands, found alongside giraffes that browse leaves in the same areas.

nodes.name: African elephant
nodes.desc: Eats grass, fruit and the leaves of mopane and ebony trees, and shapes woodland as it feeds.

nodes.name: Impala
nodes.desc: A mixed grazer and browser that is among the most common prey of lions, leopards and wild dogs.

nodes.name: Puku
nodes.desc: A floodplain antelope of grassland near water and the best-recorded large grazer in the park area.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: Herds graze coarse grass and are taken by lions, hyenas and wild dogs.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Rests in the river by day and grazes grass on land at night, moving nutrients into the water as dung.

nodes.name: Thornicroft's giraffe
nodes.desc: The Luangwa Valley giraffe browses leaves, including mopane, above where other herbivores can reach.

nodes.name: River fish
nodes.desc: Fish in the river and lagoons are fertilized by hippo dung and are eaten by crocodiles and fish eagles.

nodes.name: African wild dog
nodes.desc: A pack hunter of impala, puku, zebra and other medium-sized herbivores.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: Hunts and scavenges across the valley, feeding on many of the same animals as lions.

nodes.name: Nile crocodile
nodes.desc: Lives in the river and lagoons, eating fish and ambushing animals that come to drink.

nodes.name: African fish eagle
nodes.desc: A bird of the river and lagoons that takes fish from the surface.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.desc: Top predator of the valley, hunting zebra, buffalo, impala, puku and giraffe.

nodes.name: Leopard
nodes.desc: A solitary hunter of impala, puku and other prey; the Nsefu sector has some of the highest recorded densities in southern Africa.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Heat and light drive growth in the woodland and grassland, so water decides when plants flourish.

nodes.name: Rainy season
nodes.desc: Rains from about December to March swell the Luangwa River and green the valley; in the dry season animals crowd near water.

nodes.name: Luangwa River floods
nodes.desc: The meandering river floods the plains each wet season and leaves lagoons that keep fish, hippos and crocodiles through the dry season.

nodes.name: Valley soil
nodes.desc: Soil of the valley floor holds the mopane woodland and grassland; dung and dead matter return nutrients to it.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Beetles, termites, fungi and microbes break down dung, carcasses and dead plants and return nutrients to the soil.
